text:
alertbot: ALERT: spike detected — hosted-upstream (us-west2) 5xx rate up (42 errors / 5m). auto-incident channel created.
emma: CS: customer SaaSCo reporting repeated 503s + streaming timeouts, started ~09:12 UTC. forwarding logs. @jason can you triage?
jason: oncall here, looking. any repro from customer or a sample request?
sasha: forwarded customer's payload (sanitized): large chat + toolcall, ~12k tokens, streaming enabled, concurrency=8. they say timeouts at ~18–22s then 503.
priya: infra: seeing a restart spike in us-west2-gpu-pool around 09:11–09:18. kube events show containers OOMKilled -> CrashLoopBackOff. node dmesg shows repeated segfaults in attention kernel.
marco: runtime: which model variant? we rolled ql4 prefetch for a few Llama forks last week. might be hitting a kernel path that doesn't handle prefetch + large KV.
priya: model_id: redwood/open-llama-34b-ql4-v2 (hosted-prod). attaching a short log snippet:
```
[Fri Mar 12 09:11:42] infer_runner[12345]: runtime error: segfault at 0x7f04c0 kernel libattention.so+0x1f8b2
[Fri Mar 12 09:11:42] kernel: [UFW] Out of memory: Killed process 12345 (infer_runner) total-vm:....
[Fri Mar 12 09:11:43] kubelet: Pod redwood-infer-xyz restarted (OOMKilled)
```
jason: ok. mitigation checklist: 1) cordon affected nodes 2) route traffic off gpu-pool -> fallback pool 3) collect core + nvml logs + backtrace 4) install temporary rate limit on large streaming requests. @priya can you cordon and move routing?
priya: cordoning nodes now (node-uw2-gpu-17, node-uw2-gpu-19). updating routing policy to fallback-cpu-pool for non-enterprise customers. pushing k8s taints & drain.
emma: informed SaaSCo of temporary routing to fallback pool (they may see higher latency). CS asked for ETA and whether this will cause billing changes.
marco: pulled one core from node-uw2-gpu-17, gdb backtrace shows segfault in attention kernel during kv_prefetch:
```
#0  0x00007f04c0a1f8b2 in attention_prefetch() at libattention.cu:412
#1  0x00007f04c0a2a3f0 in run_attention (ctx=0x7ffee...) at runtime.c:223
#2  0x0000555e8a9b4c31 in infer_loop (/app/infer_runner)
```
marco: NVML shows GPU memory peak ~98% and then OOM kill. looks like prefetch + batch concurrency spikes memory beyond limits.
jason: can we reproduce locally? marco/priya, steps?
marco: repro steps (quick):
1) send stitched prompt ~12k tokens,
2) enable streaming + toolcall,
3) set client concurrency=8 and server batch cap=16,
4) observe memory climb and eventual segfault within ~15–25s.
priya: running `kubectl logs -n hosted redwood-infer-xyz -c infer-runner --since=30m` and `sudo dmesg | tail -n50` saved to s3://redwood-debug/7991002345/logs.txt
emma: CS: customer confirmation — they can tolerate rollback; ask if we can disable prefetch for their tenant immediately.
marco: short-term: disable KV prefetch for redwood/open-llama-34b-ql4-v2 and cap batch_size to 8 for hosted-prod. I can push a rollout (canary -> all) in ~40–60m. long-term: add graceful OOM handling in runtime and enforce per-request prefetch budget.
jason: proceeding with rollback + batch cap. creating incident ticket: INCIDENT-7991002345 (attention-kernel-segfault-on-prefetch-oom). tagging eng-runtime, eng-infra.
priya: rollback flag pushed to canary (subset of nodes). confirming metrics: 5xxs down by ~70% on canary, overall 5xx trending down. cordoned nodes remain quarantined for postmortem.
emma: updated SaaSCo: mitigation underway, ETA ~1h for full rollback. they requested credits if SLA breached — flagged finance. :thumbsup:
marco: uploaded core, bt, nvml dumps to s3://redwood-debug/7991002345/ (core.tar.gz, nvml.log, bt.txt). created repro harness for CI.
jason: next steps: continue rollout to remaining nodes, schedule postmortem, collect heap/profile for further analysis, and determine whether quant/ql4 prefetch change introduced regression. assigning owners in bug.
emma: CS says customers still see a handful of long-tail timeouts but 503s are much reduced. marking incident as mitigated for now; will follow up with postmortem.
alertbot: INCIDENT 7991002345 status=mitigated severity=high affected_customers=[SaaSCo]
